items.name: Even quadratic lattices, the dual lattice and the discriminant group
items.statement: (L, Q) is an integral even quadratic lattice with bilinear form (x.y) = Q(x + y) − Q(x) − Q(y), V = L ⊗ Q, L^∨ = {x ∈ V : (x.y) ∈ Z for all y ∈ L} and the discriminant group L^∨/L; det(L) is the Gram determinant. Throughout, (L, Q) has signature (b, 2) with b ≥ 3 (b ≥ 1 in §2) and rank r = b + 2.
items.note: Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean:61, Dual/Basic.lean:75, Discriminant/Group.lean:109, Even.lean:65, Signature.lean:81. Tau Ceti works with the bilinear form; IsEven (all norms (x.x) even) is the paper's "Q is Z-valued".

items.name: Maximal lattices and isotropic subgroups of the discriminant form
items.statement: L is maximal among lattices in V on which Q is Z-valued if and only if L^∨/L has no nonzero subgroup isotropic for the discriminant quadratic form; hence each L_p = L ⊗ Z_p is maximal in V ⊗ Q_p.
items.note: Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean:254 and :343, the order isomorphism between even overlattices and isotropic subgroups of the discriminant quadratic module. The passage to L_p (the p-part of L^∨/L is L_p^∨/L_p) is a one-line consequence left to the consumer.

items.name: The Clifford algebra and its Z/2-grading
items.statement: For a ring R, C(L_R) is the quotient of the tensor algebra of L_R by the ideal generated by x ⊗ x − Q(x), with the grading C(L_R) = C^+(L_R) ⊕ C^−(L_R) induced by the tensor degree mod 2; C(L) is a lattice in C(V).
items.note: Mathlib 082e2d3: LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Basic.lean:74, Grading.lean:32 and :111, Even.lean:54.

items.name: The Gauss hypergeometric function and the Gamma function
items.statement: H(a, b, c; z) = Σ_{n≥0} (a)_n(b)_n/(c)_n · z^n/n! for |z| < 1, with (a)_n = Γ(a + n)/Γ(a) [AS64, Ch. 15].
items.note: Mathlib 082e2d3: Analysis/SpecialFunctions/OrdinaryHypergeometric.lean:71 and :81 (coefficients via ascPochhammer), Gamma/Basic.lean:287.

items.name: GSpin(V), the spinor similitude and the Shimura datum
items.statement: G = GSpin(V) with G(R) = {g ∈ C^+(V_R)^× : gV_Rg^{−1} = V_R}, spinor similitude ν : G → G_m [Bas74, §3], and the exact sequence 1 → G_m → G → SO(V) → 1 (g ↦ g • v = gvg^{−1}). The period domain D_L = {[z] ∈ P(V_C) : (z.z) = 0, (z.z̄) < 0}; for z = u + iw with u, w orthogonal and Q(u) = Q(w) = −1, h_[z](i) = uw gives the Hodge decomposition V^{1,−1} = Cz, V^{−1,1} = Cz̄, V^{0,0} = (Cz ⊕ Cz̄)^⊥. (G, D_L) is a Shimura datum with reflex field Q [And96, App. 1]; [z] gives the negative definite plane P_x = span_R{u, w}.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: The GSpin Shimura variety M and its level
items.statement: K = G(A_f) ∩ C(L̂)^×, whose image in SO(L̂) is the subgroup acting trivially on L^∨/L [MP16, Lemma 2.6]. By canonical models, M is a b-dimensional Deligne–Mumford stack over Q with M(C) = G(Q)\D_L × G(A_f)/K.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: The Kuga–Satake abelian scheme and the K3-type motive
items.statement: The functor (N, N_Z) ↦ (N_B, F^•N_dR) from Q-representations of G with a K-stable lattice to variations of Z-Hodge structures on M(C). Applied to (V, L) it gives the weight-0 polarized VHS (V_B, F^•V_dR); applied to H = C(V) with left multiplication and H_Z = C(L) it gives a VHS of type (−1, 0), (0, −1), the homology of the Kuga–Satake abelian scheme A^univ → M of relative dimension 2^{b+1}, with right C(L)-action and grading A^univ = A^univ,+ × A^univ,− [MP16, 3.5–3.10]. H_dR, H_ℓ,ét descend to M; via absolute Hodge cycles [MP16, 3.4, 3.10–3.13] so do V_dR and V_ℓ,ét, embedded in End_{C(V)}(H_?) compatibly with filtration, connection and Galois action, with canonical quadratic form v ∘ v = Q(v)·Id.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Hodge-generic points
items.statement: x ∈ M(K) is Hodge-generic if for one (equivalently any) σ : K ↪ C, x^σ ∈ M(C) lies on no special divisor Z(m)(C). Equivalently λ_x ≠ 0 for every nonzero λ ∈ L (the projection to the negative plane of a lift of x). One may always pass to the smallest GSpin sub-Shimura variety containing Y_K, since each Z(m)_K is a union of GSpin Shimura varieties of signature (b − 1, 2); the Mumford–Tate group is not assumed maximal.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Special divisors over C and over Q
items.statement: For β ∈ L^∨/L and m ∈ Q(β) + Z, m > 0: Z(β, m)(C) = ⊔_{g ∈ G(Q)\G(A_f)/K} Γ_g \ (⋃_{λ ∈ β_g + L_g, Q(λ) = m} λ^⊥), with Γ_g = G(Q) ∩ gKg^{−1}, L_g = g • L. It is a union of Shimura varieties of signature (b − 1, 2) with a canonical model over Q for b ≥ 2; Z(β, m) → M is finite unramified and étale locally a closed immersion cut out by one equation, and its scheme-theoretic image is an effective Cartier divisor.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (the integral model M)
items.statement: There is a flat normal Deligne–Mumford Z-stack M with: (1) M_{Z(p)} smooth over Z_(p) when L is almost self-dual at p (self-dual, or p = 2, dim V odd and 4 ∤ |L^∨/L|); (2) A^univ extends to an abelian scheme over M with its C(L)-action; (3) F¹V_dR extends to a line bundle ω; (4) for E/Q_p finite and t ∈ M(E) with A^univ_t of potentially good reduction over O_E, t extends to Spec(O_E) → M [AGHMP18, Prop. 4.4.1, Thm. 4.4.6; HM17, Rem. 6.3.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: The integral realizations V_dR, V_ℓ,ét and V_cris at self-dual primes
items.statement: For L self-dual at p: H_dR, H_ℓ,ét extend over M_{Z(p)} as relative de Rham homology and Tate module of A^univ, and H_cris is the relative crystalline homology over M_{F_p}; V_ℓ,ét ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_ℓ,ét) extends [AGHMP18, Rem. 4.2.3]; V_dR (with integrable connection) and an F-crystal V_cris embed as local direct summands of End_{C(L)}(H_dR), End_{C(L)}(H_cris), compatibly with the crystalline–de Rham comparison [AGHMP18, Props. 4.2.4, 4.2.5].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Definition 2.2 (special endomorphisms) and their quadratic form
items.statement: For an M-scheme S, v ∈ End_{C(L)}(A_S) is special if (1) at primes p where L is self-dual, all homological realizations of v lie in the image of V_? ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_?) (? = B, dR, cris, (ℓ, ét), dropping B if S_Q = ∅; only B when p is invertible on S); (2) at p where L is not self-dual, after an isometric embedding L ↪ L^⋄ into a maximal lattice of signature (b^⋄, 2) self-dual at p, the image of v in End_{C(L^⋄)}(A^⋄_S) satisfies (1), independently of L^⋄ [AGHMP18, Props. 4.4.7, 4.5.1]. V(A_S) is the Z-module of special endomorphisms; it carries a positive definite Z-valued quadratic form with v ∘ v = Q(v)·Id [AGHMP18, Prop. 4.5.4].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Definition 2.3 (special endomorphisms of the p-divisible group)
items.statement: For S an M_{Z(p)}-scheme, v ∈ End_{C(L)}(A_S[p^∞]) is special if its crystalline realization (respectively the image under End_{C(L)}(A_S[p^∞]) ↪ End_{C(L^⋄)}(A^⋄_S[p^∞])) lies in V_cris (respectively V^⋄_cris) when L is (respectively is not) self-dual at p. The p-adic étale condition of [AGHMP18, §4.5] follows from the crystalline one by the proof of [MP16, Lemma 5.13].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Special endomorphisms as Tate classes (Madapusi Pera)
items.statement: For p odd with L self-dual at p and x ∈ M(F_{p^r}): V(A^univ_x) ⊗ Q_ℓ ≅ lim_n V_ℓ,ét,x^{Frob_x^n = 1} for ℓ ≠ p, and V(A^univ_x) ⊗ Q_p ≅ lim_n (Q_{p^{rn}} ⊗ V_cris,x)^{φ_x = 1}, as isometries [MP15, Thm. 6.4; Kis17, Cor. 2.3.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: The integral special divisors Z(m) and Z(β, m)
items.statement: For m > 0, Z(m) is the Deligne–Mumford stack over M with Z(m)(S) = {v ∈ V(A_S) : Q(v) = m}; more generally Z(β, m) parametrizes special quasi-endomorphisms [AGHMP18, §4.5], with Z(m) = Z(0, m). Its generic fibre is the divisor Z(β, m) over Q [AGHMP18, Prop. 4.5.8], and étale locally on the source it is an effective Cartier divisor on M.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Lemma 7.2 (local intersection numbers as lattice counts)
items.statement: Let Y ∈ M(O_K) with Y_K Hodge-generic, 𝔓 a prime of O_K, O^nr_𝔓 the integers of the maximal unramified extension of K_𝔓, and L_n = V(A_{O^nr_𝔓/𝔓^n}) the lattice of special endomorphisms mod 𝔓^n (L_{n+1} ⊂ L_n, ⋂ L_n = 0, positive definite Q). Then (Y.Z(m))_𝔓 = Σ_{n≥1} #{v ∈ L_n : Q(v) = m}, a finite sum. The étale local ring of Y ×_M Z(m) at v pro-represents lifts of v, so its length is the largest n such that v lifts mod 𝔓^n.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Proposition 7.3 (the lattices L_n)
items.statement: Let Λ be the Z_p-lattice of special endomorphisms of A[p^∞] over O^nr_𝔓 and e the ramification index of 𝔓. Then rank_Z L_n ≤ b + 2 and rank_{Z_p} Λ ≤ b. There is n_0 such that L_{n_0′ + ke} = (Λ + p^k L_{n_0′} ⊗ Z_p) ∩ L_{n_0} for all n_0′ ≥ n_0 and k ≥ 1; in particular r = rank L_n is independent of n. Proof via [AGHMP18, Lemma 4.5.2] (reduction to the self-dual case), Dieudonné theory, Grothendieck–Messing (Λ ⊆ F⁰V_dR ∩ V_cris^{φ=1}, with equality of rank b + 1 excluded by weak admissibility), Serre–Tate (⋂(L_n ⊗ Z_p) = Λ) and [MP16, Lemma 5.9] with the Néron mapping property, following [ST19, Thm. 4.1.1, Lems. 4.1.3, 4.3.2].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: rank L_n = b + 2 exactly at supersingular reduction
items.statement: rank L_n = b + 2 if and only if Frobenius is isoclinic on V_cris,Y_𝔓, i.e. Y_𝔓 lies in the basic (supersingular) locus of M_𝔓.
items.note: Stated without proof and not used in the proof of Theorem 7.1. Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Lemma 7.10 (lifts with prescribed p-adic special endomorphisms)
items.statement: Let y ∈ M(F_q) be the reduction of a CM point Y at an ordinary prime p not dividing the discriminant of its lattice L of special endomorphisms, with Y the canonical lift. For a self-dual Z_p-submodule Λ ⊂ L ⊗ Z_p there is a lift Y_Λ ∈ M(W(F_q)) of y with Z_p-lattice of special endomorphisms Λ, and the lattice of special endomorphisms of Y_Λ mod p^{n+1} is (Λ + p^nL ⊗ Z_p) ∩ L [Serre–Tate; MP16, Cors. 5.17, 5.19].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Siegel threefolds as GSpin Shimura varieties (b = 3)
items.statement: Via GSp_4 ≅ GSpin(V) with b = 3 [KR00], the moduli space S_2 of principally polarized abelian surfaces is a GSpin Shimura variety; for a principally polarized abelian surface B the special endomorphisms are the s ∈ End(B) with s^† = s and tr s = 0. At [B] ∈ S_2 the Kuga–Satake variety A = A^+ × A^− has dimension 2^{2+3−1} = 16, C^+(V) ≅ M_4(Q), A^+ is isogenous to B^4, and a special endomorphism induces s_B ∈ End(B) ⊗ Q with s_B^† = s_B, tr s_B = 0 [KR00, §1, Def. 2.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Assumption 1.5 and the splitting A^+ ~ B^{2^n}
items.statement: Assume b ≥ 3, b ≡ 3 mod 4 and C^+(V, Q) ≅ M_{2^n}(Q) with n = (b + 1)/2. Then every Kuga–Satake abelian variety A = A^+ × A^− parametrized by M has A^+ isogenous to B^{2^n} for an abelian variety B.
items.note: §9.2 prints dim B = 2^n; it is 2^{n−1} (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: Endomorphisms at a Hodge-generic point (van Geemen)
items.statement: Under Assumption 1.5, if [A] is Hodge-generic in M then End(A^+_K̄) ⊗ Q = C^+(V); in particular End(B_K̄) = Z and B is geometrically simple [vG08, §5.2].
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: From special endomorphisms of A to endomorphisms of B
items.statement: With an orthogonal basis e_1, …, e_{b+2} of L, Q = Σ d_ix_i², and b ≡ 3 mod 4, δ_0 = e_1⋯e_{b+2} ∈ Z(C(L)) ∩ C(L)^− satisfies δ_0^* = δ_0 and δ_0² = Π d_i. For a special v : A^+ → A^−, s = δ_0 ∘ v ∈ End_{C^+(L)}(A^+) is not a scalar, and gives a non-scalar s_B ∈ End(B) ⊗ Q.
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: An example with C^+(V) ≅ M_{2^n}(Q)
items.statement: If b ≡ 3 mod 8, the form Q(x) = −x_1² − x_2² + Σ_{i=3}^{b+1} x_i² + d x_{b+2}² has C^+(V) ≅ M_{2^n}(Q) [algorithm of vG00, Thm. 7.7].
items.note: d is not specified in the source. Hilbert-symbol computation (PARI) of the class of C^+(V) = C(−d·⟨−1, −1, 1, …, 1⟩) at ∞, 2 and the primes dividing d: trivial for b = 3, 11 and every d tested (±1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 15, −3), and nontrivial for the controls b = 5, 7. Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: From unitary Shimura varieties to GSpin Shimura varieties
items.statement: For an imaginary quadratic E, auxiliary A_0 ∈ M(1, 0) (CM by O_E) and A ∈ M(r, 1): the Hermitian forms ψ_0, ψ of signatures (1, 0), (r, 1) on W_0 = H_1(A_0(C), Q), W = H_1(A(C), Q) induce a Hermitian form of signature (r, 1) on Hom_{O_E}(W_0, W), and V = Hom_{O_E}(H¹_B(A_0), H¹_B(A)) with tr_{E/Q} of it has signature (2r, 2). With G′ ⊂ GU(W_0) × GU(W) the pairs of equal similitude, G′ → SO(V) is a morphism of Shimura data [BHK+17, §§2.1, 6.2; Hof14, §4], Sh(G′) ⊂ M(1, 0) × M(r, 1) [BHK+17, Prop. 2.2.1], and after a Hecke translate there is Y ∈ M(Q) with V_B,Y ⊗ Q ≅ Hom_{O_E}(H_1,B(A_0), H_1,B(A)). By Deligne's theorem on absolute Hodge cycles, after a finite extension of K, V_ℓ,ét,Y ≅ Hom_{O_E}(H_1,ét(A_0, Q_ℓ), H_1,ét(A, Q_ℓ)) as Galois modules (9.1).
items.note: Routed to the Part II OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (parent ShimuraVarieties).

items.name: The moduli stacks M(r, 1) and M(1, 0)
items.statement: M(r, 1) over O_E: triples (B, ι, λ) of an abelian scheme B/S, ι : O_E ↪ End_S(B) with ι(a)^† = ι(a^σ), and a principal polarization λ, such that ι(a) acts on Lie with characteristic polynomial (T − φ(a))^r(T − φ(a)^σ); a Deligne–Mumford stack whose generic fibre is a disjoint union of GU(r, 1) Shimura varieties [KR14, Props. 2.19, 4.4]. M(1, 0) likewise.
items.note: M1 plans PEL moduli functors with the determinant (Kottwitz) condition; M5 plans a unitary PEL example with specified signatures.

items.name: Serre–Tate and Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory
items.statement: Deformations of an abelian scheme (with endomorphisms) over a nilpotent thickening are deformations of its p-divisible group, and over PD-thickenings they are lifts of the Hodge filtration.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 7.3 and Lemma 7.10, pp.37–38, 42
items.note: A4 plans the Serre–Tate equivalence with endomorphism structures and imports Grothendieck–Messing from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.6.

items.name: The Néron mapping property
items.statement: Used, with [MP16, Lemma 5.9] and [AGHMP18, Lemma 4.5.2], to show that an endomorphism of A over O^nr_𝔓/𝔓^n is special iff its reduction is.
items.note: R11.1 plans Néron models and the mapping property.

items.name: The Weil representation ρ_L and vector-valued modular forms
items.statement: ρ_L : Mp_2(Z) → Aut_C(C[L^∨/L]) is the unitary Weil representation on the basis (𝔢_β) [Bru02, §1.1]; M_{1+b/2}(ρ_L) is the space of C[L^∨/L]-valued holomorphic modular forms of weight k = 1 + b/2 [Bru02, Def. 1.2]. The paper's Q is −1 times that of [Bru02, BK03], so their Weil representation is replaced by its dual.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Harmonic weak Maass forms and Hejhal–Poincaré series
items.statement: H_{2−k}(ρ_L^∨) is the space of vector-valued harmonic weak Maass forms of weight 2 − k for ρ_L^∨ [BY09, 3.1]. For β ∈ L^∨/L, m ∈ Z + Q(β), m > 0, F_{β,m} ∈ H_{2−k}(ρ_L^∨) is the Hejhal–Poincaré series F_{β,−m}(τ, 1/2 + b/4) of [Bru02, Def. 1.8].
items.note: Routed to QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3 as a source.

items.name: Borcherds–Bruinier Green functions and arithmetic special divisors
items.statement: Φ_{β,m} is the regularized theta lift of F_{β,m} in the sense of Borcherds [Bru02, (2.16); BF04, §5.2]; it is a Green function for Z(β, m) [Bor98, §6, Thm. 13.3; Bru02, §2.2, (3.40), Thm. 3.16], descending from D_L to M(C). Ẑ(β, m) = (Z(β, m), Φ_{β,m}); Φ_m = Φ_{0,m} and Ẑ(m) = Ẑ(0, m).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Arithmetic Chow groups, the metrized ω and heights of O_K-points
items.statement: CĤ¹(M)_Q is the Gillet–Soulé arithmetic Chow group [GS90] as in [AGHMP17, §4.1], and Pic^(M)_Q ⊗ Q ≅ CĤ¹(M)_Q since M is a normal Deligne–Mumford stack [Sou92, III.4]; Ẑ(β, m) ∈ Pic^(M)_Q. ω carries the Petersson metric ‖z‖² = −(z.z̄)/(4πe^γ), γ = −Γ′(1). For Y = Spec O_K → M, the height h_Ẑ(Y) (respectively h_ω(Y)) is the image of Ẑ (respectively ω) under CĤ¹(M)_Q ≅ Pic^(M)_Q → Pic^(Y)_Q →(deg^) R [AGHMP17, §§5.1–5.2; AGHMP18, 6.4].
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The decomposition (3.1) of h_Ẑ(m)(Y)
items.statement: If Y_K is Hodge-generic, then Y ×_M Z(m)(S) = {v ∈ V(A_S) : v ∘ v = [m]} and h_Ẑ(m)(Y) = Σ_{σ : K ↪ C} Φ_m(Y^σ) + Σ_𝔓 (Y.Z(m))_𝔓 log|O_K/𝔓|, where (Y.Z(m))_𝔓 = Σ_{v ∈ Y ×_M Z(m)(F̄_𝔓)} length(O_{Y ×_M Z(m), v}) (3.2).
items.note: (8.2) weights the archimedean terms by 1/|Aut(Y^σ)|, which (3.1) and (8.1) omit. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 3.1 (Howard–Madapusi Pera modularity)
items.statement: Assume b ≥ 3. The formal generating series Φ_L = ω̂^∨𝔢_0 + Σ_{β ∈ L^∨/L} Σ_{m > 0, m ∈ Q(β)+Z} Ẑ(β, m) q^m 𝔢_β lies in M_{1+b/2}(ρ_L) ⊗ Pic^(M)_Q: for every Q-linear α : Pic^(M)_Q → C, α(Φ_L) ∈ M_{1+b/2}(ρ_L) [HM17, Thm. 9.4.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The Eisenstein series E_0(τ, s) and its coefficients c(β, m)
items.statement: E_0(τ, s) is the Eisenstein series of [BK03, (1.4), (3.1)] with β = 0, κ = 1 + b/2; it converges normally for Re(s) > 1 − k/2 and is Mp_2(Z)-invariant. Its Fourier expansion is Σ_β Σ_{m ∈ Q(β)+Z} c_0(β, m, s, y) e^{2πimx}𝔢_β with c_0(β, m, s, y) = C(β, m, s) W_s(4πmy) for m ≠ 0 [BK03, Props. 3.1, 3.2, (3.22), (3.2)]. E_0(τ) = E_0(τ, 0) = 2𝔢_0 + Σ_{m > 0} c(β, m)q^m𝔢_β ∈ M_{1+b/2}(ρ_L), with C(β, m, 0) = c(β, m); C(m, s) = C(0, m, s), c(m) = c(0, m).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Signs, size and explicit formula of c(m)
items.statement: c(β, m) encodes deg Z(β, m)(C) [BK03, Prop. 4.8]; c(β, m) < 0 if m ∈ Q(L + β) and c(β, m) = 0 otherwise [BK01, Prop. 14]; for m ∈ Q(L + β), |c(β, m)| ≍ m^{b/2} [Tay20a, Ex. 2.3] (3.4). Explicitly c(m) = −2(2π)^{b/2+1} m^{b/2} / (√|L^∨/L| Γ(b/2 + 1)) · Π_p μ_p(Q, m) [BK01, (19), (22), (23)].
items.note: The factor 2 matches the constant term 2𝔢_0 of E_0: for L = U² ⊕ E_8 (b = 10, unimodular) the formula gives c(m) = −1008σ_5(m), which is 2 × (−504σ_5(m)) from E_6. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Coefficient bound for vector-valued cusp forms
items.statement: For a cusp form g ∈ M_{1+b/2}(ρ_L), the m-th coefficient of its 𝔢_0-component satisfies |g(m)| ≤ C_{ε,g} m^{(2+b)/4+ε} [Sar90, Prop. 1.5.5].
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 3.2 (asymptotics of the global height)
items.statement: For every ε > 0 and m ∈ Z_{>0}: h_Ẑ(m)(Y) = −(c(m)/2) h_ω(Y) + O_ε(m^{(2+b)/4+ε}); in particular h_Ẑ(m)(Y) = O(m^{b/2}). Proof: by Theorem 3.1 and [Bru02, p.27], −h_ω(Y)𝔢_0 + Σ h_Ẑ(β,m)(Y)q^m𝔢_β = −(h_ω(Y)/2)E_0 + g with g a cusp form.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Local counts N_m(p^n), densities μ_p(m, n) and w_p(m)
items.statement: N_m(p^n) = #{v ∈ L/p^nL : Q(v) ≡ m mod p^n}, μ_p(m, n) = p^{−n(r−1)} N_m(p^n) (4.1); w_p(m) = 1 + val_p(m) for p ≠ 2 and w_2(m) = 1 + 2val_2(2m). The local density is μ_p(Q, m) = lim_k μ_p(m, k), which stabilizes for k ≫ 1.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Jordan splitting of a maximal L_p and Hanke's solution types
items.statement: (L_p, Q) = ⊕_j (L_j, p^{ν_j}Q_j) with (L_j, Q_j) unimodular of rank 1 or 2 (rank 1 if p ≠ 2) [Han04, (2.3), Lemma 2.1]; maximality of L_p forces ν_j ≤ 1. S_i = {j : ν_j = i}, s_i = #S_i. A solution v ∈ N_m(p^n) is of zero type if v ≡ 0 mod p, of good type if v_j ≢ 0 mod p for some j with ν_j = 0, and of bad type otherwise; μ^good, μ^bad, μ^zero are the corresponding densities; Q′ replaces each ν_j by 1 − ν_j. N_m = N_m^good when p ∤ m; N_m^zero(p^n) = ∅ when p² ∤ m and n ≥ 2; N_m^bad = ∅ when p ∤ 2det(L) [Han04, Def. 3.1, Rem. 3.4.1].
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.2 (Hanke's reduction maps)
items.statement: Let δ = 2val_2(p) + 1. (1) For n ≥ δ and all m, μ_p^good(m, n) = μ_p^good(m, δ). (2) If p | m (L maximal): N^bad_{m,Q}(p^{n+1}) = p^{r−s_0} N^good_{m/p,Q′}(p^n), i.e. μ^bad_{p,Q}(m, n + 1) = p^{1−s_0} μ^good_{p,Q′}(m/p, n). (3) If p² | m: N^zero_m(p^{n+2}) = p^r N_{m/p²}(p^n), i.e. μ^zero_p(m, n + 2) = p^{2−r} μ_p(m/p², n) [Han04, Lemma 3.2, pp.359–360].
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 4.3 (closed formulas for μ_p(m, n), p odd)
items.statement: For p ≠ 2, with δ_{p,det(L)} = 1 if p | det(L) and 0 otherwise: (1) if n ≥ val_p(m) + 1, μ_{p,Q}(m, n) = Σ_{u=0}^{⌊val_p(m)/2⌋} p^{(2−r)u} μ^good_{p,Q}(m/p^{2u}, 1) + δ_{p,det(L)} p^{1−s_0} Σ_{u=0}^{⌊(val_p(m)−1)/2⌋} p^{(2−r)u} μ^good_{p,Q′}(m/p^{2u+1}, 1); (2) if 1 ≤ n ≤ val_p(m) with n odd, μ_{p,Q}(m, n) = p^{(2−r)(n−1)/2} μ_{p,Q}(mp^{1−n}, 1) + Σ_{u=0}^{(n−3)/2} p^{(2−r)u} μ^good_{p,Q}(m/p^{2u}, 1) + δ_{p,det(L)} p^{1−s_0} Σ_{u=0}^{(n−3)/2} p^{(2−r)u} μ^good_{p,Q′}(m/p^{2u+1}, 1); (3) the analogous formula for n even.
items.note: Part (1) was checked by brute force for Q = x_1x_2 + x_3x_4 + 3x_5² (p = 3, n = 3, all m < 27): no mismatch. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.4 (stabilization of μ_p(m, n))
items.statement: For every prime p, integer m and n ∈ {2 + val_2(p), …, w_p(m) − 1}: |μ_p(m, n) − μ_p(m, w_p(m))| ≪ p^{−(3⌊n/2⌋ − 2)}, with an absolute implied constant.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.5 (densities at good primes are close to 1)
items.statement: There is C_2 > 0 such that for all m, n > 0 and all primes p ∤ 2det(L): |μ_p(m, n) − 1| ≤ C_2/p. (Via Corollary 4.3, Lemma 4.4 and the Weil bound for the smooth quadric Q ≡ 0 or m mod p [Wei49; Del74, Thm. 8.1].)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.6 (a uniform lower bound)
items.statement: Since r ≥ 5 and L is maximal, μ_p(m, n) ≥ 1/2 for all m, n > 0 and all primes p: in some basis of L_p, Q = x_1x_2 + Q_1(x_3, …, x_r) [Ger08, Lemma 6.36], so μ_p^good(m, δ′) ≥ (p − 1)/p for 1 ≤ δ′ ≤ δ.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.1 (the local term in the Bruinier–Kühn formula)
items.statement: If m is representable by Q over Z, then |w_p(m) − Σ_{n=0}^{w_p(m)−1} μ_p(m, n)/μ_p(m, w_p(m))| ≪ 1/p, with the implied constant independent of p and m.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 7.9 (a discriminant-sensitive bound on local densities)
items.statement: For an integral positive definite quadratic form Q of rank r ≥ 5, m ≥ 1 and a prime p: μ_∞(Q, 1)μ_p(Q, m) ≪_r p^r / |Disc(Q)|^{3/20}. Proof: μ_∞(Q, 1) ≍_r Disc(Q)^{−1/2}; Hanke's decomposition μ_p = μ^good + μ^bad1 + μ^bad2 + μ^zero [Han04, §3, pp.359–360] with μ^good ≤ p³, μ^bad1 ≤ p⁴, μ^bad2/Disc(Q)^{1/2} ≤ p^{2−r}μ″_p(m/p², n − 2)/Disc(Q″)^{1/2}, μ^zero ≤ p^{2−r}μ_p(m/p², n − 2), Disc(Q″) ≥ Disc(Q)/p^{2r}, and induction on n.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Singular integral, Siegel masses and the singular series
items.statement: For an integral quadratic form F in n ≥ 5 variables with nonzero discriminant and a weight ω: μ_∞(F, ω) = lim_{ε→0} (1/2ε)∫_{|F(x)−1|≤ε} ω(x)dx (the limit exists for ω ∈ C(S) [HB96, pp.154–155]); μ_p(F, m) = lim_k p^{−(n−1)k} #{x mod p^k : F(x) ≡ m}; μ(F, m) = Π_p μ_p(F, m), absolutely convergent for n ≥ 5 [Iwa97, §11.5].
items.note: Routed to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 as a source.

items.name: Heath-Brown's weight classes C(S) (Remark 4.8)
items.statement: Smooth compactly supported weights ω : R^n → C and the classes C(S) of [HB96, §2]. (1) There is ω_0^{(n)} ∈ C(n) with values in [0, 2], support in [−1, 1]^n and ω_0^{(n)} ≥ 2 on [−1/2, 1/2]^n (rescaling [HB96, (2.1), (2.2)]). (2) If M is invertible with the entries of M and M^{−1} bounded by K and ω ∈ C(S), then ω(Mx) ∈ C(S, K) [HB96, p.162]. N(F, m, ω) = Σ_{x ∈ Z^n, F(x) = m} ω(x/√m).
items.note: Routed to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.9 (Heath-Brown)
items.statement: For F an integral quadratic form in n ≥ 5 variables with nonzero discriminant, m ≠ 0 and ω ∈ C(S): N(F, m, ω) = μ_∞(F, ω)μ(F, m)m^{n/2−1} + O_{F,S,ε}(m^{(n−1)/4+ε}); the error depends only on F and S [HB96, Thm. 4].
items.note: Routed to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 4.10 (Heath-Brown, positive definite forms)
items.statement: If moreover F is positive definite: #{x ∈ Z^n : F(x) = m} = μ_∞(F, 1)μ(F, m)m^{n/2−1} + O_{F,ε}(m^{(n−1)/4+ε}) [HB96, Cor. 1].
items.note: Routed to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 4.7 (every large m is represented)
items.statement: Every sufficiently large m ∈ Z_{>0} is represented by (L, Q): choose ω ≥ 0 with μ_∞(Q, ω) > 0; Lemma 4.6 gives μ(Q, m) > 0, so N(Q, m, ω) > 0 for m large by Theorem 4.9.
items.note: Positivity of N needs μ(Q, m) ≫ m^{−(b−1)/4+ε}, which follows from Lemma 4.6 at the primes dividing 2m·det(L) and μ_p(m, 1) = 1 + O(p^{−2}) elsewhere; the proof only says "by the Proposition above". Routed to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 as a source.

items.name: Niedermowwe's count in expanding regions
items.statement: For a nondegenerate integral quadratic form in n ≥ 5 variables, the number of representations of m by lattice points in homogeneously expanding rectangular regions equals singular integral × singular series × m^{n/2−1} plus an error with explicit dependence on the expansion parameter [Nie10, Thm. 3.6]; the singular series agree with [HB96], and for smooth weights Nie10's I_ω(m) = m^{b/2}μ_∞(Q, ω) (footnote 24).
items.note: Routed to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 as a source.

items.name: The measure μ_∞ on L_{R,1}, the regions Ω_{≤T} and the weights a(m), h_s
items.statement: L_{R,1} = {λ ∈ L_R : Q(λ) = 1} with μ_∞(W ∩ L_{R,1}) = lim_{ε→0} (1/2ε) μ_L({λ ∈ W : |Q(λ) − 1| < ε}) (4.5), μ_L the Lebesgue measure giving L covolume 1. For x ∈ D_L with negative plane P and projections λ_x, λ_{x⊥}: Ω_{≤T} = {λ ∈ L_{R,1} : −Q(λ_x) ∈ [0, T]}. a(m) = −c(m)Γ(k)√|L^∨/L| / (2(2π)^k) ≍ m^{b/2} (4.6), and h_s(λ) = (1 − Q(λ_x))^{−(k−1+s)}.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 4.11 (volume of Ω_{≤T})
items.note: Rederived: the change of variables factor 2^{1+b/2}/√|L^∨/L| and the shell integral give 2ε((1 + T)^{b/2} − 1) times the prefactor. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 4.12 (upper bound for T ≤ 1)
items.statement: For m ∈ Z_{>0} and 0 < T ≤ 1: #{λ ∈ L : Q(λ) = m, λ/√m ∈ Ω_{≤T}} = O_Q(m^{b/2}T) + O_{Q,T,ε}(m^{(b+1)/4+ε}) (Theorem 4.9 with ω = ω_P(λ_x)ω_{P⊥}(λ_{x⊥}) ∈ C(b, T) and μ(Q, m) = O(1)).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.13 (asymptotic for T ≥ 1)
items.statement: Let A > 1. For m ∈ Z_{>0} and T ≥ 1: #{λ ∈ L : Q(λ) = m, λ/√m ∈ Ω_{≤T}} = a(m)μ_∞(Ω_{≤T}) + O(m^{b/2}T^{b/2}(log mT)^{−A}). Niedermowwe's proof [Nie10, Thm. 3.6] "carries over without change" to these regions; then use the formula for c(m).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 4.14 (integral of h_s)
items.note: Rederived. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Bruinier's explicit series φ_m(x, s) and its regularization φ_m(x)
items.statement: For Re(s) > k/2 and a lift x ∈ D_L: F(s, z) = H(s − 1 + k/2, s + 1 − k/2, 2s; z) and φ_m(x, s) = (2Γ(s − 1 + k/2)/Γ(2s)) Σ_{λ ∈ L, Q(λ) = m} (m/(m − Q(λ_x)))^{s−1+k/2} F(s, m/(m − Q(λ_x))) (5.3) [Bru02, (2.15), with a different regularization]. It continues meromorphically to Re(s) > 1 with a simple pole at s = k/2 of residue −c(m) [Bru02, Prop. 2.8, Thm. 2.14; BK03, Prop. 4.3]; φ_m(x) = lim_{s→k/2}(φ_m(x, s) + c(m)/(s − k/2)) is its constant term (5.4) [BK03, Prop. 4.2].
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The function b_m(s)
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 5.1 (Bruinier)
items.statement: For x ∈ D_L: Φ_m(x) = φ_m(x) − b′_m(k/2) [Bru02, Prop. 2.11]; in particular φ_m is also a Green function for Z(m).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 5.3 (Bruinier–Kühn)
items.statement: Let D be the fixed integer of Theorem 2.4, d = (−1)^{r/2}det(L) if r is even and 2(−1)^{(r+1)/2}D det(L) if r is odd, d_0 the fundamental discriminant of Q(√d), and L^{(p)}_m(t) = N_m(p^{w_p})t^{w_p} + (1 − p^{r−1}t)Σ_{n=0}^{w_p−1} N_m(p^n)t^n. For all m representable by (L, Q) with m/D a square: b′_m(k/2)/b_m(k/2) = log(m) + 2σ′_m(k)/σ_m(k) + O(1), where σ_m(s) = Π_{p | 2m det(L)} L^{(p)}_m(p^{1−r/2−s})/(1 − χ_{d_0}(p)p^{−s}) for r even and Π_{p | 2m det(L)} (1 − χ_{d_0}(p)p^{1/2−s})/(1 − p^{1−2s}) · L^{(p)}_m(p^{1−r/2−s}) for r odd (5.6) [BK03, Thm. 4.11, (4.73), (4.74)].
items.note: The published proof takes logarithmic derivatives in (5.5) and uses that d_0 and k do not depend on m. For b odd and m/D not a square, d_0 varies with m; see sourceIssues E1. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Mertens's first theorem and Σ_{p | N} log p/p = O(log log N)
items.statement: Σ_{p<X} log p/p = log X + O(1); hence for N ≥ 2, Σ_{p | N} log p/p ≤ log log N + O(1) (split at X = log N).
items.note: Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (b′_m(k/2))
items.statement: Let m ∈ Z_{>0} with Z(m) ≠ ∅, and if b is odd assume m/D is a square (D fixed as in Theorem 2.4). As m → ∞, b′_m(k/2) = |c(m)| log m + o(c(m) log m); in particular b′_m(k/2) ≍ m^{b/2} log m. Proof: Lemma 5.3, the χ_{d_0}-terms are bounded (k ≥ 5/2), and the L^{(p)}_m-terms are ≤ C/p by Proposition 4.1, giving σ′_m(k)/σ_m(k) = O(log log m).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The singular quantity A(m, x)
items.statement: For Hodge-generic x ∈ M(C) with a lift to D_L: A(m, x) = −2 Σ_{√mλ ∈ L, Q(λ) = 1, |Q(λ_x)| ≤ 1} log|Q(λ_x)| = 2 Σ_{λ ∈ L, Q(λ) = m, |Q(λ_x)| ≤ m} log(m/|Q(λ_x)|) (5.7). It is independent of the lift, a finite sum (the region is compact and λ_x ≠ 0 by Hodge-genericity), and non-negative.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The decomposition φ_m(x) = φ̃_m(x, 0) + R_x(0, m)
items.statement: With F(s, z) = zG(s, z) + 1: φ̃_m(x, s) = (4/b) Σ_{√mλ ∈ L, Q(λ) = 1} (1 − Q(λ_x))^{−(k+s)} G(k/2 + s, 1/(1 − Q(λ_x))) and R_x(s, m) = c(m)/s + (4/b) Σ_{√mλ ∈ L, Q(λ) = 1} (1 − Q(λ_x))^{−(k−1+s)}. φ̃_m(x, s) is holomorphic near s = 0, R_x(s, m) continues holomorphically to s = 0, and φ_m(x) = φ̃_m(x, 0) + R_x(0, m) (5.8)–(5.9); the Gamma ratio of (5.3) tends to 2/b. By Lemma 4.14, R_x(s, m) = (4/b)Σ h_s(λ) − (4a(m)/b)∫ h_s dμ_∞ for s > 0.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 5.5 (bounding R_x(0, m))
items.statement: For Hodge-generic x ∈ D_L: R_x(0, m) = lim_{s ∈ R_{>0}, s→0} R_x(s, m) = O(m^{b/2}). Proof: sum over shells Θ_N = Ω_{≤N+1} \ Ω_{≤N}, where h_s = (N + 1)^{−(s+k−1)} + O((N + 1)^{−(s+k)}), and use Proposition 4.13 and Lemma 4.11 with partial summation.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 5.6 (φ̃_m(x, 0))
items.statement: φ̃_m(x, 0) = A(m, x) + O(m^{b/2}). Proof: G(s + k/2, z) is bounded for |s| ≤ ε ≤ 1/2, |z| ≤ 1/2, handling |Q(λ_x)| > 1 as in (5.10); for z ∈ [1/2, 1), |z^kG(k/2, z) + (b/2)log(1 − z)| ≤ C since G(k/2, z) = Σ_{n≥1} (k − 1)/(n + k − 1) z^{n−1}; and #{√mλ ∈ L : |Q(λ_x)| ≤ 1} = O(m^{b/2}).
items.note: Checked numerically (mpmath) that z^kG(k/2, z) + (b/2)log(1 − z) stays bounded on [1/2, 1) for b = 3, 4, 7, 10. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 5.4
items.statement: For m ∈ Z_{>0}: φ_m(x) = A(m, x) + O(m^{b/2}). (From (5.9) and Propositions 5.5–5.6.)
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 5.7 (archimedean asymptotic)
items.statement: For every m representable by (L, Q): Φ_m(Y^σ) = c(m) log m + A(m, Y^σ) + o(|c(m)| log m). (Propositions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4.)
items.note: As proved, only for m/D a square when b is odd (sourceIssues E1). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 5.8 (uniform diophantine bounds)
items.statement: For every positive integer m: (i) 0 ≤ A(m, Y^σ) ≪ m^{b/2} log m; (ii) (Y.Z(m))_𝔓 log|O_K/𝔓| ≪ m^{b/2} log m; (iii) Σ_{σ : K ↪ C} Φ_m(Y^σ)/|Aut(Y^σ)| = O(m^{b/2} log m). Proof: (3.1), Proposition 3.2 and Proposition 5.2 give Σ_𝔓 (Y.Z(m))_𝔓 log|O_K/𝔓| + Σ_σ φ_m(Y^σ) ≍ m^{b/2} log m, and every term is ≥ −O(m^{b/2}).
items.note: Used in Proposition 6.4 for arbitrary M = Q(λ) and in Lemma 7.6 for m = a_1(n)²; the proof covers only m/D a square when b is odd (sourceIssues E1). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Logarithmic asymptotic density
items.statement: For S ⊂ Z_{>0}, the logarithmic asymptotic density of S is limsup_{X→∞} log|S_X|/log X, where S_X = {a ∈ S : X ≤ a < 2X}.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 6.2 (main term via the circle method)
items.statement: Write A(m) = A_mt(m) + A_er(m), the sums over 1 ≤ |Q(λ_x)| ≤ m and 0 < |Q(λ_x)| < 1. Then lim_{m→∞} A_mt(m)/(m^{b/2} log m) = 0. Proof: split at |Q(λ_x)| = m/T and apply Corollary 4.12 to both pieces: A_mt(m) ≪ m^{b/2} log T + m^{b/2}(log m)/T + O_T(m^{(b+2)/4} log m).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (a pigeonhole lemma for the negative plane)
items.statement: Let C > 2, X > 1 and N ≥ 2. If S ⊂ L_R has N vectors with C ≤ Q(v) ≪ X and |Q(v_x)| < e^{−C}, then there are v ≠ v′ in S with w = v − v′ satisfying (1) −log|Q(w_x)| ≫ min(−log|Q(v_x)|, −log|Q(v′_x)|) and (2) Q(w_{x⊥}) ≪ X/N^{2/b}, with absolute implied constants.
items.note: The proof's last step prints Q(v_{x⊥} − v′_{x⊥}) ≤ T² where 2T is the minimal distance; it should be (2T)² (sourceIssues E5, harmless). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 6.4 (the error term outside a sparse set)
items.statement: The set S_bad of m with A_er(m) > m^{b/2} (6.3) has logarithmic asymptotic density zero. Proof: for ε ∈ ]0, 1[, S_bad ∩ ]X, 2X] ⊂ B_{1,X} ∪ B_{2,X} ∪ B_{3,X} (many λ with |Q(λ_x)| < 1; one λ with −log|Q(λ_x)| ≥ X^{b/2}; many λ in a dyadic range ]Z_i, 2Z_i]), and |B_{1,X}| = O(X^ε) by geometry of numbers, |B_{2,X}| ≪ log X and |B_{3,X}| ≪ X^ε log X by Lemma 6.3 with Theorem 5.8(i).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 6.1
items.statement: There is S_bad ⊂ Z_{>0} of logarithmic asymptotic density zero with A(m) = o(m^{b/2} log m) for every m ∉ S_bad (Propositions 6.2 and 6.4).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Successive minima (Definition 7.4)
items.statement: For a lattice L_n of rank r with positive definite Q and 1 ≤ i ≤ r: μ_i(n) = inf{y > 0 : there are linearly independent v_1, …, v_i ∈ L_n with Q(v_j) ≤ y²}; a_i(n) = Π_{j≤i} μ_j(n), a_0(n) = 1 [EK95].
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1/GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Successive minima and the discriminant
items.statement: For a positive definite lattice of rank r, a_r ≍_r Disc^{1/2} [EK95, (5), (6)] (Minkowski's second theorem).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1/GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Counting lattice points by successive minima
items.statement: For a positive definite lattice of rank r: #{v ≠ 0 : Q(v) < X} ≪_r Σ_{i=0}^r X^{i/2}/a_i [EK95, Lemma 2.4, (5), (6); Sch68].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.7, p.40 and footnote 32

items.name: Corollary 7.5 (successive minima of L_n)
items.statement: Every successive minimum satisfies μ_j(n) ≪ p^{n/e}. If r = b + 2 then a_{b+1}(n) ≫ p^{n/e} and a_{b+2}(n) ≫ p^{2n/e}. Proof: L_n = (Λ + p^{(n−n_0)/e}L_{n_0} ⊗ Z_p) ∩ L_{n_0} with n_0 bounded and n_0 ≡ n mod e, so [L_1 : L_n] ≫ p^{2k}, k = (n − n_0)/e.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 7.6 (lower bound from the diophantine bound)
items.statement: For every ε > 0: a_1(n) ≫_ε n^{1/(b+ε)} and a_i(n) ≫_ε n^{i/(b+ε)}. Proof: a vector w_0 ∈ L_n with Q(w_0) = a_1(n)² lies in L_k for all k ≤ n, so n ≤ (Y.Z(a_1(n)²))_𝔓 ≪_ε a_1(n)^{b+ε} by Lemma 7.2 and Theorem 5.8(ii).
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 7.7
items.statement: (1) If r = rank L_n ≤ b + 1, then Σ_{n≥1} #{v ∈ L_n \ {0} : Q(v) < X} = O(X^{(b+1)/2}). (2) If r = b + 2, then Σ_{n ≥ ⌈(e/4) log_p X⌉} #{v ∈ L_n \ {0} : Q(v) < X} = O(X^{(b+1)/2}). (Lemma 7.6 cuts the sum at n ≍ X^{(b+ε)/2}; the counting lemma; Corollary 7.5 for the i = b + 2 term.)
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 7.1 (finite places on average)
items.statement: Let D ∈ Z_{≥1} and S_{D,X} = {m ∈ Z_{>0} : X ≤ m < 2X, m/D ∈ Z ∩ (Q^×)²}. For a fixed prime 𝔓 of O_K: Σ_{m ∈ S_{D,X}} (Y.Z(m))_𝔓 = o(X^{(b+1)/2} log X). Proof: Proposition 7.7; for n ≤ (e/4)log_p X split at n = eT and apply Corollary 4.10 to L_1 and L_{eT} with Lemma 7.9 (μ_∞(Q_T, 1)μ(Q_T, m) ≪ p^{−3T/5}). Remark 7.8: for Theorem 1.8 one may sum over all m.

items.name: Lemma 7.11 (a criterion for exponential intersection numbers)
items.statement: Suppose a self-dual Z_p-sublattice Λ ⊂ L ⊗ Z_p of rank r ≥ 5 satisfies (1) Λ ∩ L = {0}, and (2) there are rank r sublattices L_i ⊂ L with discriminants D_i and Λ ≡ L_i mod p^{N_i} with N_i ≥ e^{e^{D_i}}. Then there are perfect squares m_i → ∞ with (Y_Λ.Z(m_i))_p exponential in m_i: L_i represents a square m_i < e^{D_i}, and (Y_Λ.Z(m_i))_p > N_i by Lemmas 7.2 and 7.10.
items.note: (2) is printed with L_{n_i} for L_i (sourceIssues E4). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: A transcendental point with exponential intersection numbers
items.statement: For a lattice of even rank ≥ 12 and a prime p, there is Y′ ∈ M(W(F_q)), not defined over a number field, with (Y′.Z(m))_p exponential in m for infinitely many perfect squares m (similarly for m ∈ D·(Q^×)²). Construction: Λ = span_{Z_p}{e_i + μf_i} for an orthogonal basis e_1, f_1, …, e_c, f_c of L (c = b/2 ≥ 5) and an irrational μ ∈ Z_p very well approximated by integers.
items.note: Illustrative; not used for the main results. The printed choice of μ does not give property (2) of Lemma 7.11 (sourceIssues E2). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 2.4 (main theorem with a fixed D)
items.statement: Assume b ≥ 3. Let K be a number field, D ∈ Z_{>0} represented by (L, Q), and Y ∈ M(O_K) with Y_K Hodge-generic. Then there are infinitely many places 𝔓 of K such that Y_𝔓 lies in the image of Z(Dm²) → M for some m ∈ Z_{>0} (m may depend on 𝔓). Equivalently, if A over O_K is a Kuga–Satake abelian scheme parametrized by M with A_K having no special endomorphisms, infinitely many A_𝔓 have a special endomorphism v with v ∘ v = [Dm²]. Proof (§8): otherwise sum (8.1) over m ∈ S_{D,X} \ S_bad (≍ X^{1/2} values): the archimedean part is ≍ −X^{(b+1)/2} log X by Theorems 5.7 and 6.1, the finite part o(X^{(b+1)/2} log X) by Theorem 7.1, contradicting Proposition 3.2.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 1.8 (main theorem)
items.statement: Let K be a number field and Y ∈ M(O_K) with Y_K ∈ M(K) Hodge-generic (b ≥ 3). Then for infinitely many finite places 𝔓 of K, Y_𝔓 lies in the image of Z(m) → M for some m ∈ Z_{>0} depending on 𝔓. It follows from Theorem 2.4.
items.note: The cases b = 1, 2 are [Cha18, ST19] (footnote 1). The assumption that Y extends over O_K is removed in [Tay22] (published as Algebra Number Theory 19 (2025), 77). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (abelian surfaces)
items.statement: Every 2-dimensional abelian scheme over O_K has infinitely many places of geometrically nonsimple reduction.
items.note: §9.2 writes the argument for End(B_K̄) = Z (a Hodge-generic point of S_2, b = 3). A principal polarization may be assumed after an isogeny (footnote 34). Surfaces with extra endomorphisms lie on smaller GSpin sub-Shimura varieties (§1.4); b ≤ 2 is [Cha18, ST19]. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (Kuga–Satake factors)
items.statement: Under Assumption 1.5, if B extends to an abelian scheme over O_K (so A does too), then B_𝔓 is geometrically nonsimple for infinitely many finite places 𝔓. Proof: take D = Π d_i, multiplied by a square to be represented (Corollary 4.7). A special v with v ∘ v = [Dm²] gives s_B = δ_0 ∘ v with s_B ∘ s_B = [D²m²], not a scalar, so ker(s_B − [Dm]) is a proper nonzero abelian subvariety; conclude by Theorem 2.4.
items.note: The proof calls ker(s_B − [Dm]) "a nontrivial simple factor"; it need not be simple (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 1.7 (unitary Shimura varieties)
items.statement: Let E be imaginary quadratic and A a principally polarized abelian scheme over O_K with O_E ⊂ End(A) compatible with the polarization, acting on Lie A_K with signature (r, 1). Then for infinitely many finite places 𝔓 of K, A_𝔓 has a geometric isogeny factor that is an elliptic curve with CM by E. Proof: the K-point Y of M from §9.3 has potentially good reduction everywhere ([And96, Lemma 9.3.1] and (9.1)), so extends by Proposition 2.1(4); by Theorem 1.8, V_ℓ,ét,Y_𝔓 has a Tate class for infinitely many 𝔓, so Hom_{O_E}(H_1,ét(A_0), H_1,ét(A))^{Frob^n = 1} ≠ 0 and A_{0,𝔓} is an isogeny factor of A_𝔓 by Tate's theorem.
items.note: Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Tate's isogeny theorem over finite fields
items.statement: For abelian varieties A, B over a finite field F_q and ℓ ∤ q: Hom(A, B) ⊗ Q_ℓ ≅ Hom_{Gal}(V_ℓA, V_ℓB).
items.note: Routed to FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4 as a source.

items.name: The transcendental GSpin datum of a K3 surface
items.statement: For a K3 surface X over a number field K with Pic(X_K̄) = Pic(X) and σ : K ↪ C: H²(X^an_σ, Z) with the cup-product form is even unimodular of signature (3, 19); c_1 : Pic(X) → H² is a primitive embedding; by the Hodge index theorem Pic(X) has signature (1, ρ(X) − 1). With (L, Q) a maximal lattice orthogonal to Pic(X) in H²(X^an_σ, Q), (L, −Q) is even of signature (b, 2), b = 20 − ρ(X), with genus independent of σ and L; M is the GSpin Shimura variety of (L, −Q). The resulting point is Hodge-generic by the Lefschetz (1, 1) theorem.
items.note: Routed to the new roadmap K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness.

items.name: The Hodge index theorem for surfaces
items.statement: On a smooth projective surface the intersection form on Pic has signature (1, ρ − 1).
items.note: SF.5 plans the Hodge index theorem for smooth projective surfaces.

items.name: André's Kuga–Satake results for K3 surfaces
items.statement: (a) Up to extending K, the Kuga–Satake abelian variety A of X is defined over K and gives x ∈ M(K) [And96, Main Lemma 1.7.1]. (b) If X has everywhere good reduction then, up to extending K, A has potentially good reduction everywhere [And96, Lemma 9.3.1], so x extends to Y ∈ M(O_K) by Proposition 2.1(4). (c) A special endomorphism s of A_𝔓 with s ∘ s = [m] corresponds to a line bundle on X_𝔓 of self-intersection −m orthogonal to the image of Pic(X) under specialization [And96, Main Lemma 1.7.1(ii)].
items.note: Routed to the new roadmap K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (Picard rank jumps)
items.statement: Let X be a K3 surface over a number field K admitting, after a finite extension of K, a smooth projective model X → Spec(O_K). Then ρ(X_𝔓̄) > ρ(X_K̄) for infinitely many finite places 𝔓 of K.
items.note: Proof by Theorem 1.8 with b = 20 − ρ(X); b ≤ 2 is [Cha18, ST19] (footnote 1). [Tay22] removes the good-reduction hypothesis. Routed to the new roadmap K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness.

items.name: Li–Liedtke's criterion for infinitely many rational curves
items.statement: If a K3 surface over a number field has infinitely many specializations whose geometric Picard rank jumps and only finitely many unirational specializations, the hypotheses of [LL12, Prop. 4.2] hold and the proof of [LL12, Thm. 4.3] gives infinitely many rational curves on X_K̄.
items.note: Routed to the new roadmap K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness.

items.name: Corollary 1.3 (rational curves)
items.statement: Let X be a K3 surface over a number field K with potentially good reduction everywhere. Then either X_K̄ contains infinitely many rational curves, or X has infinitely many unirational, hence supersingular, specializations.
items.note: The rational-curve conjecture (Conjecture 1.2) is proved in characteristic 0 in [CGL19, Thm. A]. Routed to the new roadmap K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness.
